openingMemo: Cleveland is the first file tonight. New England leads my Sunday morning; Seattle leads the afternoon. New Orleans is where I want to start Monday. Chicago and the Giants have bigger-looking gaps than some of those games, but each still has an unanswered input.

The weekly rating update is incomplete. These are Graham’s retained bases with the changes already included in his current numbers; the larger disagreements still need checking. I have six priorities below. No order on this copy.
scheduleMemo: Pittsburgh at Cleveland opens Thursday at 17:15. Indianapolis–Washington is Sunday’s 06:30 neutral-site start, followed by eight games at 10:00, one at 13:05, three at 13:25 and Detroit at Carolina at 17:20. Atlanta at New Orleans closes Monday at 17:15. All times Pacific.
changeMemo: This is the first Week 4 sheet. The September 22 Week 3 edition stays in the archive; its matchups and prices are closed.

All sixteen Week 4 Graham numbers and Pinnacle spread comparisons are on this copy. Cleveland’s fair carries an October 1, 11:41 timestamp; the other fairs retain their individual timestamps. Washington and Chicago still carry quarterback-input warnings. The remaining personnel questions stay beside their game reads.

Pinnacle spread comparison: October 1, 09:25 Pacific. Graham board captured October 1, 11:46 Pacific; its information-review timestamp is September 30, 16:54 Pacific. A refreshed board timestamp does not turn those quotes or observations into new reports.

reviews.read: Cleveland is tonight’s first file. Graham makes the Browns a one-point favorite; the benchmark has them getting three. I like the direction of that disagreement, but Cleveland’s offensive-line configuration and Pittsburgh’s secondary roles still need answers. The reserve running-back estimate is already in Graham’s number—don’t count it twice.
reviews.note: Browns first tonight. Get the line and secondary answers before trusting the four-point gap.

reviews.read: Washington gets a second look, not a place at the top of my list. Graham has Indianapolis by one and a half against four on the benchmark; the saved market change gives Washington another half-point. This is a neutral-site game, and Washington’s quarterback input still carries an unresolved warning.
reviews.note: Early Sunday deadline. Keep the quarterback question beside the number.

reviews.read: I’m not spending much time on a one-point Baltimore disagreement yet. The center group in Baltimore and guard configuration in Tennessee remain open questions; they matter more to this read than the small gap.
reviews.note: Finish the two line questions. Don’t dress up one point.

reviews.read: New England is my first Sunday-morning review. Graham has Buffalo by two and a half; the benchmark asks seven. Four and a half points toward the Patriots earns a proper look, especially with no separate personnel or quarterback warning on this matchup’s sheet.
reviews.note: Patriots near the top. The disagreement is worth the work.

reviews.read: I’m leaving Chicago outside the main watchlist. Nine on Graham’s sheet against three on the benchmark is a six-point disagreement, but Chicago’s quarterback input is still unresolved here. A large difference doesn’t answer that question for me.
reviews.note: Quarterback first. Six points can wait.

reviews.read: Jacksonville has the modest underdog comparison here: Cincinnati by one on Graham’s sheet against two and a half on the benchmark. It belongs in the second pass through Sunday, behind the larger disagreements.
reviews.note: Jacksonville gets another look after the first files are finished.

reviews.read: Dallas interests me because the two columns disagree on the favorite. Graham makes the Cowboys a half-point favorite; the benchmark has Houston by three. The saved market change adds half a point to Houston’s favoritism while Graham’s saved fair is unchanged, but Houston’s defensive-tackle rotation still needs sorting.
reviews.note: Cowboys on the watchlist. Resolve the Houston rotation; keep the two numbers separate.

reviews.read: The Giants have the biggest gap on the sheet: Graham makes them four-point favorites while the benchmark gives them two and a half. That earns attention, but the unresolved edge rotation keeps them behind my cleaner first reviews. I want the pass-rush answer before leaning hard on six and a half points.
reviews.note: Largest gap, unfinished personnel read. Those are two different things.

reviews.read: Philadelphia’s extra point is a quiet comparison. Graham has the Rams by two and the benchmark has them by three; I’m keeping this below the main watchlist.
reviews.note: Small Philadelphia difference. Later in the morning review.

reviews.read: Green Bay stays on my secondary list. Five and a half on Graham’s sheet against three and a half on the benchmark leaves two points toward the Packers. Useful, but smaller than the first Sunday files.
reviews.note: Packers second pass. Keep the current number; don’t carry last week’s questions forward.

reviews.read: Miami gets a small comparison, not priority treatment. Minnesota is nine and a half on Graham’s sheet against eleven on the benchmark, while Miami’s backfield and Minnesota’s tight-end workload remain unresolved inputs.
reviews.note: One and a half points doesn’t settle the workload questions.

reviews.read: Las Vegas stays on my afternoon list. Graham has Kansas City by one and a half against four and a half on the benchmark: three points toward the Raiders, with no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded for this matchup. It is a straightforward disagreement worth revisiting.
reviews.note: Raiders after Seattle. Keep the favorite’s name out of the arithmetic.

reviews.read: Seattle is my first afternoon file. Graham makes thirteen while the benchmark asks seven and a half; five and a half points is too much disagreement to leave unread. There is no separate personnel or quarterback warning on this matchup’s sheet, though the unfinished weekly rating update still applies.
reviews.note: Seahawks lead the afternoon review. Check the retained rating base before treating the gap as settled.

reviews.read: San Francisco is only a point apart, but the two columns sit on opposite sides of three. I’ll give that a price check after the larger afternoon files, without pretending it is the same case as Seattle.
reviews.note: Small gap, important part of the spread. Keep it in the second pass.

reviews.read: Carolina has a useful comparison: Graham makes the game even while the benchmark favors Detroit by three and a half. I’m keeping it conditional because Carolina’s guard replacement and secondary configuration are still unresolved. The number alone isn’t enough to move it ahead of my first files.
reviews.note: Panthers need the personnel answers before Sunday night.

reviews.read: New Orleans is my first Monday review. Graham has the Saints by seven against three on the benchmark, four points toward the home side, with no separate quarterback or personnel warning recorded for this matchup. There is time to check the disagreement again before Monday’s kickoff.
reviews.note: Saints at the front of the Monday file. Recheck the number before the late deadline.

closingWatchlist: 1. CLEVELAND — Tonight’s first review. Browns −1 on Graham’s sheet against +3 on the benchmark. Four points and a favorite reversal, subject to the line and secondary answers.
2. NEW ENGLAND — First Sunday-morning file. Buffalo −2.5 against −7 leaves four and a half points toward the Patriots. No separate quarterback or personnel warning is recorded for this matchup.
3. SEATTLE — First afternoon file. Thirteen against seven and a half gives the Seahawks the largest disagreement among my first reviews. Check the retained rating base before relying on it.
4. NEW ORLEANS — First Monday file. Saints −7 against −3 is a four-point disagreement, with time to revisit it before kickoff.
5. DALLAS — The columns disagree on the favorite: Dallas −0.5 against Houston −3. Houston’s defensive-tackle rotation is the outstanding question.
6. LAS VEGAS — Kansas City −1.5 against −4.5 leaves three points toward the Raiders. My next afternoon review after Seattle.

The Giants remain a conditional review until the edge rotation is settled. Chicago stays outside the main ranking while its quarterback input is unresolved. Washington has the early Sunday deadline; Carolina’s guard and secondary questions matter before Sunday night. No order.
signature: Those are my first files. The rest can wait their turn. — Bill
currentMood: Reserved and direct. Cleveland first tonight; New England, Seattle, New Orleans, Dallas and Las Vegas lead the Week 4 review priorities. Giants, Chicago, Washington and Carolina keep their unresolved questions. Retained rating bases remain visible. No order.
